era_setting.place: rural Pennsylvania (Weimer/open-fields tracts) and Middle Tennessee
era_setting.notes: The open-fields cases this episode follows are contemporary: the Pennsylvania Game Commission trespass suits and the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency litigation run 2019 through the present, so modern vehicles, phones, computer screens and present-day signage are all IN PERIOD here. What is OUT of period is the place: this is rural US farmland and woodland, and a European park, EU plates, foreign-language signage or a city street are all wrong for it. Declared because EP62 greene shipped a modern ballot and a Range Rover Evoque on an EU plate through five green gates, purely because nothing machine-readable said what century or continent the film was in.

forbidden_subjects: PROSE RULE (not filename-matchable, for the writer and for Codex): no likeness of any REAL person -- not the named landowners, not the officers, not the judges. Generated people DO show their faces; a generated face is nobody's likeness, and the owner decided on 2026-07-04 that depicted people are fine and only a real individual's likeness is barred (invariant 11). The 20 PEOPLE plates L235-L254 are deliberately face-forward and are ordered as generic people using land, never tied to a named party in the record -- tying one to a named party is how a fictional face becomes a claim about a real person. The film had no human being in it until minute eleven before these were ordered.

PROSE RULE: no readable text, numeral, handwriting, seal, emblem or logo burned into any GENERATED plate. This episode's most dangerous plate class is the posted boundary sign: a generator asked for a posted sign will write POSTED or NO TRESPASSING on it. Posted boundaries are ordered as a weathered blank placard, a colour, a shape and a purple paint blaze -- never as lettering. Real signage that happens to be legible inside ARCHIVE footage is a different question and is decided at footage QC, not here.

PROSE RULE: no depiction of any officer's state of mind -- no plate staging someone sneaking, hiding, smirking, watching through glass, or otherwise dramatising a motive. The opinions record conduct, not intent (see forbidden_claims).

PROSE RULE: no identifiable real property. No plate may carry a real farm's name, a real road number, a real county seal or an architecture distinctive enough to place it. Ordinary Appalachian and Middle Tennessee farmland only.

PROSE RULE: no hunting-kill imagery. This is a property-rights film, not a hunting film. A hunting club is the plaintiff, so the register is gates, tracks, cameras and boundaries -- never a shot animal, never a rack of guns.

PROSE RULE: no surveillance-thriller styling. No green night-vision wash, no crosshairs, no CCTV-monitor grid, no thermal false colour. The trail camera is a small dull plastic box strapped to a trunk, and that is the whole point of it.
forbidden_claims: The figure that 96% (or "nearly all", or "almost every acre") of private land in the United States lies outside Fourth Amendment protection under the open-fields doctrine. IT IS UNVERIFIABLE FROM THIS MACHINE: the Institute for Justice page that carries it returns HTTP 403 and no other primary source for it is in this repository. Not in narration, not in a caption, not in an on-screen figure, not in the thumbnail, not in the description. If a primary, retrievable source is later obtained and recorded in the facts ledger with its retrieval date, this entry is amended -- it is not quietly dropped.

Any percentage, acreage, or count of landowners, cameras, entries, states or agencies, from any source, unless it appears in EP66_openfields_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md with a primary citation. This episode's whole subject invites invented magnitude.

Any statement about what the officers wanted, believed, suspected, intended or were trying to achieve, beyond conduct the opinions themselves record. "They were spying on him", "they wanted to intimidate him", "they targeted the club", "they knew they needed a warrant" are all forbidden. Conduct: they entered; the land was posted and gated; they installed cameras. That is what may be said.

That the entries were illegal, unconstitutional or a crime under FEDERAL law. Under Hester v. United States (1924) and Oliver v. United States (1984) the Fourth Amendment does not reach open fields; that is the doctrine the episode is about. Any holding for the landowners in these two cases rests on a STATE constitution, and the script must keep the two levels apart in every sentence.

That the United States Supreme Court has decided, reviewed, granted certiorari in, or declined either Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pennsylvania Game Commission or Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency.
That either decision changed the law outside its own state, ended the open-fields doctrine, or binds any other state's courts.

Any statement of what either court HELD, of its disposition, of its vote, of its author, or of any judge's reasoning -- until EP66_openfields_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md exists and records it verbatim against the opinion text. THAT LEDGER DOES NOT EXIST YET (TODO, see notes). Until it does, the correct number of asserted holdings in any draft is zero.

Merging the two cases. Different states, different courts, different constitutions, different parties, different years (Tenn. Ct. App., 9 May 2024; Pa. Supreme Court, 21 July 2026). "The courts ruled", "both landowners won the same thing", "the two cases said" are forbidden constructions.
Any statement about what happened next to the named parties -- appeals, damages, whether the cameras came down, whether anyone was prosecuted -- unless it is in the ledger with a citation.

RUNTIME -- 1620-1980 s, the mid profile (27-33 min)
=====================================================================
docs/PD_ONE_PASS_PRODUCTION_SPEC.v2.md line 14 and scripts/check_final_acceptance.py line 39 both define mid = 27-33 min. 27 x 60 = 1620; 33 x 60 = 1980. The measured comparable channel runs 22-39 min, so 27-33 sits inside the comparable band with room on both sides rather than at an edge. This is WIDER than EP65 marmet's [1620, 1920]; nothing about marmet's narrower top was derived, and 33 min is the profile's own ceiling.

=====================================================================
SCRIPT_WORDS -- 4565-5247, DERIVED, SHOW THE ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================
Do NOT use 176 wpm. docs/PD_CANON.md section 7 rule 25: "176 words/min is optimistic. Measured 159.5-169.7. Design the runtime from the measured VO." An independent in-repo datapoint agrees: EP65 marmet's finished ElevenLabs master ffprobes at 1896.2 s for 5,133 narration words = 0.36941 s/word = 162.4 wpm, inside that band.

Non-narration overhead, measured on the same episode: the delivered film is 1902.2 s (09_package/final_delivery.v001.json) against a 1896.2 s narration master = +6.0 s, 0.3 percent. So narration seconds available = runtime - 6.

The band is built so that BOTH edges are legal across the WHOLE measured pace range, not at one assumed pace:

  low  = (1620 - 6) x 169.7 / 60 = 1614 x 2.828333 = 4564.9 -> 4565 words
         (at the FASTEST measured read, a 4,565-word script still fills 27:00)
  high = (1980 - 6) x 159.5 / 60 = 1974 x 2.658333 = 5247.5 -> 5247 words
         (at the SLOWEST measured read, a 5,247-word script still ends before 33:00)

Cross-check at the opposite pace: 4,565 words at 159.5 wpm = 1717 s = 28.6 min (in band); 5,247 words at 169.7 wpm = 1855 s = 30.9 min (in band). So any word count in [4565, 5247] lands inside [1620, 1980] at any pace in [159.5, 169.7].

Why the old figure over-filled: at 176 wpm the same runtime band would read [4734, 5790]. A 5,790-word script at the slowest measured pace is 5790 / 159.5 x 60 = 2178 s = 36.3 min -- three minutes past the ceiling. That is the mechanism that produced the over-length films on the previous slate.

=====================================================================
TARGET_CUT_SEC -- 3.5, and WHY the number alone will not save the film
=====================================================================
The failure being prevented: EP65 marmet failed acceptance on a 4.03 s near-still hold caused by looping a 4.8 s i2v motion clip into a longer slot (scripts/check_motion_clip_stillness.py header). i2v clips are 4.80 s. Any slot longer than 4.80 s loops the clip, and a looped near-still clip reads as frozen.

HOW A SLOT LENGTH IS ACTUALLY PRODUCED (scripts/build_case_film_generic.py):
  * L396-410: want = total_sec / target_cut_sec  (the constant 4.6 cancels out of the scaling).
  * L186-205 solve_totals: the cut count is then CAPPED at 2 x (distinct video pool) + 1 x (still pool), with the video share targeted at MIN_VIDEO_SHARE = 0.68.
  * L437-447: slot = section_seconds x weight / sum(weights), footage weight 3.343, still weight 3.000.

WHAT MARMET ACTUALLY MEASURED (remotion/src/data/marmet_film.json, read for this contract):
  396 cuts over 1881.7 s = 4.752 s average. Footage slots: median 4.870 s, max 5.046 s.
  312 footage cuts from 156 distinct sources = exactly 2 x 156, the reuse cap.
  84 still cuts from 84 distinct stills = exactly 1 x 84, the still cap.
  At target_cut_sec 3.7 the builder ASKED for 1881.7 / 3.7 = 509 cuts. The pool could supply 396.

So marmet's 4.87 s slots were not caused by declaring 3.7. They were caused by the pool saturating 22 percent below the requested cut count. Lowering target_cut_sec in a saturated build changes nothing at all: want rises, min(want, pool cap) does not. THIS IS THE IMPORTANT PART OF THIS SECTION.

CHOOSING THE VALUE, from that measurement rather than from the model:
  observed worst-case inflation = longest footage slot / declared cut = 5.046 / 3.7 = 1.3638
  3.5 x 1.3638 = 4.773 s  <= 4.80  PASS
  3.6 x 1.3638 = 4.910 s  >  4.80  FAIL
3.5 is therefore the largest one-decimal value whose LONGEST slot still fits inside a 4.80 s clip even if EP66's pool falls short by exactly the same proportion marmet's did. Declared: 3.5.

With a pool that is NOT short, the slot is target x 3.343 / (3.0 + 0.343 x f), where f is the footage share of cuts: at marmet's measured f = 0.788 that is 1.0222 x 3.5 = 3.58 s; at the builder's minimum video share f = 0.68 it is 1.0340 x 3.5 = 3.62 s. For reference, the mathematical ceiling for a non-looping 4.80 s clip with a fully supplied pool is 4.80 / 1.0340 = 4.64 s -- 3.5 sits far below it deliberately, because the binding term is the pool, not this number.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFENCE (do not rely on this field alone): run
  py -3.11 scripts/check_motion_clip_stillness.py --slug openfields
over the motion pool BEFORE the build and quarantine every clip whose longest still stretch exceeds 3.0 s. target_cut_sec stops the looping; that tool stops the clip that was near-still to begin with. marmet needed both.

=====================================================================
DISTINCT_VIDEO_ASSETS -- 350, DERIVED, AND ITS PRICE
=====================================================================
At the mid profile's 30:00 design target (1800 s, the centre of the runtime band) and 3.5 s cuts:
  1800 / 3.5 = 514.3 -> 514 cuts
  video cuts = ceil(514 x 0.68) = 350        (MIN_VIDEO_SHARE = 0.68)
  still cuts = 514 - 350 = 164, which equals floor(350 x 0.32 / 0.68) = 164, so the two agree.
docs/PD_EPISODE_SPEC_STANDARD.v001.md is explicit that this field is FOOTAGE CUTS, not cuts divided by the reuse cap. Declared: 350.

The price, stated so nobody discovers it after a render:
  * scripts/check_episode_inputs.py computes need = 350 // 2 = 175 ACCEPTED archive clips as a hard pre-flight floor, and warns that asset_reuse will fail unless accepted + motion >= 350.
  * check_spec_satisfied.py fails the build if the film carries fewer than 350 distinct video sources.
  * marmet declared 234, shipped 156, and carries asset_reuse red for exactly that reason.

TODO -- the archive/motion split is NOT derivable yet and is deliberately not guessed here. Woodland, farmland, gates, fence lines and gravel tracks are a register the shelf may cover far better than marmet's care-home interiors did, which is why 350 is plausible for this subject and was not for that one. Measure it, per register, with:
  py -3.11 scripts/search_archive.py --shot "<register>" --kind video --md --sheet
then visually QC and count. Plate budget then follows arithmetically:
  i2v motion plates needed = 350 - (accepted archive clips)
  still plates needed      = 164
Batch B's size is that subtraction. It is not a number this file can hold.

IF the measurement shows the pool cannot reach 350, there are exactly two legal responses and both are owner decisions, not silent edits: (a) commission the missing plates; or (b) raise target_cut_sec -- at 4.6 the slot is 4.6 x 1.0340 = 4.756 s, still under 4.80 with a supplied pool, and distinct_video_assets re-derives to ceil(1800 / 4.6 x 0.68) = 267. Do not take (b) and leave this field at 350, and do not take (b) while the pool is still short -- that is how marmet got 4.87 s slots.

PEOPLE_PLATES / PEOPLE_PLATES_MIN -- 10
=====================================================================
The standard's floor is 8; EP62-65 all declared 10 and the measured siblings carry 7-16. This film's protagonists are landowners, so a thin people register would be the EP57 failure again (2 people plates in a film about one person). Ten faceless plates are ordered as L056-L065 and declared in people_plates, because check_episode_inputs counts declared ids rather than guessing from the filename prefix.

THUMBNAIL_CANDIDATES_MIN -- 4, raised from the standard's 3
=====================================================================
Measured floors the finished thumbnail must clear: mean luma >= 33.0 and contrast (luma stddev) >= 40.0 (check_final_acceptance THUMB_MIN_MEAN_LUMA / THUMB_MIN_CONTRAST_STD), plus subject-region mean luma >= 60, a tallest-4-connected-component height >= 150 px at 1280 px width, and a dark outline >= 12 px (check_thumb_subject_luma). An overcast woodland subject fights all of those the way marmet's low-key interior did -- marmet had to add a fifth thumbnail plate (R224) late, under hard key light, precisely because its own [STYLE] collided with the luma floor. Ordering four bright, hard-lit THUMB plates up front and declaring four is cheaper than discovering it at the gate.
